The Mem is the linguistic/symbolic body of the Accuser — when separated from the protective verse and allowed to join the Name SAL, it transforms SAL into SAMael. This node requires an edge: אות מ"ם ↔ סמ"ך-מ"ם.

This requires an edge: מם של מות ↔ אות מ"ם.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: Pinchas is mentioned as the Zoharic witness who saw the Mem of death circling. He is not established as a bechina-concept in this Torah — he is the observer of the bechina, not a bechina node himself. Excluded per framework strictness: no בחינת language applied to Pinchas in this teaching.

Death is mentioned as the context from which God saves the person (line 1: 'לְהַצִּיל אוֹתוֹ מִמָּוֶת שֶׁנִּגְזַר עָלָיו') and in the phrase 'מֵ"ם שֶׁל מָוֶת.' However, מות itself is not declared a bechina of anything — it is the referent of the decree, not a node connected by explicit bechina language. The Mem OF death is a node (מם של מות), but death itself is background context. Excluded.

The Torah opens with 'מָּוֶת שֶׁנִּגְזַר עָלָיו' (death that was decreed upon him). The decree is background context setting up why the Name's protection is needed. No bechina language is applied to גזרה itself. Excluded.

The full name 'סַמָּאֵל' appears in line 3 as the dangerous combination formed when Mem joins SAL. It is the outcome/result of the Accuser's victory, not a separate conceptual node from סמ"ך-מ"ם. In Torah discourse, 'סמ"ך-מ"ם' and 'סמאל' are the same entity — the convention of not fully spelling out the name is itself part of the Torah's teaching. Treated as the same node as סמ"ך-מ"ם rather than a separate bechina node. Noted but not added as a separate node.
The word צֵרוּף appears in line 3 to describe the dangerous joining of letters. It is a technical term for the process, not a bechina-concept node. No בחינת language applies to צרוף itself. Excluded.
